sourcedFrom: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) (2024)
cleanIntro: A striker-fired, short-recoil 9 mm with a modified linkless Browning lock, 4.09 inch barrel and a 7.34 inch overall length. Its field strip needs no tools at all, and it is gated by a mechanical disassembly safety: the lever will not rotate until the magazine is out and the slide is locked back. HK's VP SERIES book covers the VP9 alongside the VP40 and the subcompact VP9SK, with separate specification tables for each.

steps.title: Point it safe, magazine out, slide locked back
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction and finger outside the trigger guard, then depress either side of the ambidextrous magazine release and take the magazine out of the well. Grasp the REAR serrations, rack the slide fully back, and push up on either slide release to lock it there. Watch the ejection port as it goes — a cartridge or case should come out if one was chambered.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out before the slide is racked, not after. Racking first strips a fresh round out of the magazine and puts you back where you started.
steps.quote: 2. Remove the magazine. Depress either side of the ambidextrous magazine release. Remove the magazine from the magazine well. 3. Open and lock the slide to the rear. Grasping the rear serrations, rack the slide to the rear while keeping the muzzle pointed in a safe direction. Push upwards on either side of the ambidextrous slide release and lock the slide to the rear.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 4 — CLEARING PROCEDURES, p.11
steps.warn: The firearm is not empty or unloaded until the magazine is removed and the chamber is clear.

steps.title: Inspect the chamber by eye AND by finger
steps.action: With the slide locked back, look through the open ejection port at the chamber, then physically insert a finger through the port and sweep the chamber and feed ramp area. Remove anything you find. HK asks for both because a case rim in a dark chamber is easy to miss and impossible to mistake by touch.
steps.prose: The feed ramp sweep is the part people skip. A round that failed to chamber can sit there without ever reaching the chamber proper.
steps.aside: The three numbered sub-steps that follow are: visually inspecting the chamber through the open ejection port; physically inserting a finger through the ejection port and sweeping the chamber and feed ramp area; and removing any cartridges or empty cases.
steps.quote: 4. Inspect the chamber. Inspect the chamber for the presence of a cartridge or empty case by:
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 4 — CLEARING PROCEDURES, p.11

steps.title: The disassembly safety will not let you cheat this
steps.action: Before you reach for the lever, understand what is holding it. The VP has a mechanical disassembly safety: with a magazine in the well — loaded or not — it is pivoted up and blocks the disassembly lever entirely, and with the slide forward the bottom of the slide blocks it too. So the lever only moves when the magazine is out AND the slide is locked back.
steps.prose: If the lever will not rotate, do not force it. It is telling you the pistol is not in the state it needs to be in, and that is the whole point of the feature.
steps.caution: A lever that will not turn is a diagnosis, not an obstacle.
steps.quote: The disassembly safety ensures that the magazine must be removed from the magazine well, the chamber be cleared, and the firing pin decocked prior to disassembly. The disassembly safety is pivoted upwards by the presence of a magazine (loaded or unloaded) and thus blocks the operation of the disassembly lever.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 3 — Safety Features, p.10

steps.title: Rotate the disassembly lever down to six o'clock
steps.action: With the slide still locked to the rear and the magazine out, rotate the disassembly lever on the LEFT-hand side of the frame downward until it points to approximately the six o'clock position. It is a positive rotation with a definite stop; take it all the way rather than most of the way.
steps.prose: A lever left short of six o'clock will not release the slide, and the temptation is then to pull harder on the slide instead of finishing the lever.
steps.quote: 2. With the slide still locked to the rear and the magazine removed, rotate disassembly lever, located on the left-hand side of the frame, downward until the lever is pointing to approximately the six o'clock position (see Figure 18).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Release the slide and push it forward off the frame
steps.action: Depress the slide release and push the slide FORWARD off the top of the frame. It does not come off backwards and it does not need to be pulled — with the lever down, the slide simply runs off the front of the rails.
steps.prose: Keep a hand over the slide as it leaves. There is nothing under spring tension yet, but a dropped slide lands on its sights.
steps.quote: 3. Depress the slide release and push the slide forward, removing the slide from the top of the frame (see Figure 19).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Recoil spring out to the side, not straight up
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down and carefully push the recoil spring FORWARD and then out to either the left or the right side, separating it from the barrel and slide. It is under compression, so control it as it comes clear — forward first, then sideways, is the sequence that releases it without launching it.
steps.prose: Doing this over a bench rather than a carpet is worth the trouble. The guide rod's rear end is what disengages, and it is small.
steps.caution: Compressed spring. Forward, then out, both hands.
steps.quote: 4. Turn the slide upside down and carefully push the recoil spring forward and out to either the left or right side, separating the recoil spring from the barrel and slide (see Figure 20).
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.20

steps.title: Barrel out through the ejection port
steps.action: Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on the barrel LOCKING BLOCK through the ejection port. That lifts the block clear of its recess in the slide and the barrel comes out. Pressing anywhere else on the barrel just binds it.
steps.prose: The locking block is the lug under the chamber that engages the ejection port cut. Finding it through the port with a thumb is the whole trick to this step.
steps.quote: 5. Pivot the barrel slightly forward and press upward on the barrel locking block through the ejection port, separating the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — DISASSEMBLY, p.21

steps.title: ⛔ Never use a steel bore brush in a VP
steps.action: When you clean the bore, use a BRONZE bristle brush of the correct calibre and nothing harder. HK's barrels are polygonal rather than cut-rifled, and a steel brush scratches the polygonal bore and costs accuracy. Six passes chamber to muzzle with a solvent-moistened bronze brush, then patches.
steps.prose: This is the one cleaning instruction in the book that is specific to how HK makes barrels rather than generic gun care.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Do not use a steel bore brush which can scratch the polygonal bore and reduce accuracy.
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — CLEANING & MAINTENANCE, p.26

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have four groups: slide, barrel with locking block, recoil spring assembly, and frame. HK's own line is that no tools are required for a user field strip and that anything past this — the detailed strip — needs punches and is depot-level work. Cleaning is Normal after every firing or every twelve months, and Major after 500 cartridges or after exposure to sand, dust, water or other contaminants.
steps.prose: Do not go further. There is nothing behind the frame rails an owner is meant to reach on this pistol.
steps.quote: No tools required for user field strip. Magazine must be removed for disassembly. Minimal tools (simple punches) required for detailed depot level disassembly
steps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 2 — Specifications (VP9/VP9-B/VP9 OPTIC READY/VP40/VP40-B), p.7

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Know which magazine release you have before you start
deepSteps.action: The VP ships with either the ambidextrous paddle release behind the trigger guard or a reversible push button, and HK states that these are MODEL SPECIFIC and not convertible in either direction. The push-button variant can be swapped left to right with a punch or a pen; the paddle variant cannot be converted to a button at all.
deepSteps.prose: This is the coverage bound on a book that covers many VP variants: your pistol is one of them and the procedure only exists for one of them.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: The paddle magazine release and the reversible push button are model specific. An HK VP handgun with a paddle magazine release cannot be converted to a push button magazine release. The push button magazine release model cannot be converted to a paddle magazine release. This determination must be made at time of purchase, as the two models are not convertible.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 7 — PUSH BUTTON MAGAZINE RELEASE, p.33

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off — a punch and a hand over the base
deepSteps.action: For a high-capacity magazine, use a punch to depress the locking plate in the floorplate and HOLD it there. Put a hand over the base of the magazine to control the spring, then slide the floorplate FORWARD off the housing. Let the locking plate and spring expand out gradually rather than releasing them.
deepSteps.prose: HK's own caution is about the force in that spring. A 17-round magazine spring at full compression will clear a bench.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Using a punch, depress the locking plate located in the floorplate and hold it there (see Figure 25). 2. Place a portion of either hand over the base of the magazine to control the release of the magazine spring and locking plate. 3. Slowly slide the floorplate forward off the mag­az­ ine housing (see Figure 26).
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — MAGAZINE DISASSEMBLY, p.23
deepSteps.warn: WARNING: Always keep the base of the mag­az­ ine point­ed in a safe direction (away from the face and eyes).

deepSteps.title: Slide, spring, barrel, frame, magazine — the five-part scrub
deepSteps.action: Nylon toothbrush moistened with solvent over all internal surfaces of the slide, then a rag and cotton swabs to lift the loose fouling. Bronze bore brush through the barrel six passes chamber to muzzle, then patches, then the toothbrush over the exterior of the barrel and locking block. Frame: concentrate on the area normally covered by the slide. Magazine: the follower and feed lips.
deepSteps.prose: The area under the slide is where fouling accumulates on a striker gun, because there is no hammer channel to take it.
deepSteps.quote: • Moisten a bronze bore brush with solv­ ent and scrub the bore from chamber to muzz­ le at least six (6) pass­es, back and forth.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — Normal Cleaning, p.26

deepSteps.title: Major cleaning is the same, plus the magazine and a full immersion
deepSteps.action: After 500 cartridges, or after sand, dust, water — salt water especially — or other visible contaminants, HK escalates: the magazine is disassembled for cleaning and all parts are rinsed or immersed in solvent and scrubbed with a nylon brush, then dried with compressed air or a rag and swabs. Everything must be thoroughly dried before it goes back together and lubricated afterwards.
deepSteps.prose: Note what HK warns against here: ultrasonic cleaning can strip the coloured reference markings off the frame, extractor and control lever, and is not normally necessary under 10,000 rounds.
deepSteps.caution: CAUTION: Use of ultrasonic cleaning machines can result in the unwanted re­mov­al of colored reference markings of the frame, extractor and control lever (where applicable).
deepSteps.quote: Major Cleaning - Major Cleaning is the same as normal cleaning ex­cept that: • The magazine is dis­as­semb­ led for cleaning. • All parts should be rinsed with or immersed in solv­ ent and thoroughly scrubbed with a nylon brush.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — Major Cleaning, p.27

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Do not modify anything you have just taken apart
deepSteps.action: HK closes the inspection section with a flat prohibition: do not alter any part of the pistol or magazine, including attempts to improve it. Altering parts may cause serious injury or death, damage the pistol, and voids the warranty. That covers trigger work as much as it covers filing a magazine catch.
deepSteps.prose: On a pistol whose only user-serviceable interfaces are the ones above, anything that requires modification is the wrong answer to whatever problem prompted it.
deepSteps.quote: WARNING: Do not alter any of the parts or components of the pistol or magazine, e.g., do not attempt to “improve” or make the pistol “better” by altering parts or components.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — INSPECTION, p.27
deepSteps.warn: Altering parts voids the warranty and may cause serious injury or death.

deepSteps.title: Magazine back together — follower, spring, locking plate, floorplate
deepSteps.action: Put the follower on the spring with the end of the spring positioned to the LEFT of the follower, then insert both into the housing. Place the locking plate on the protruding end of the spring with its rounded corners facing the FRONT of the magazine, push it into the housing against spring pressure and hold it there while the floorplate slides on.
deepSteps.prose: Both orientations matter and neither is obvious: spring end to the left, rounded corners forward.
deepSteps.caution: Check the follower slides freely and rises nearly flush against the feed lips before the magazine is trusted.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Place the magazine follower onto the magazine spring with the end of the spring positioned on the left of the follower.
deepSteps.cite: OPERATOR'S MANUAL — VP SERIES — ALL MODELS AND CALIBERS — Jan 2024 (imprint page) — Section 5 — MAGAZINE ASSEMBLY, p.25

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Gently scrub all internal surfaces with a nylon toothbrush moistened with solvent
Remove all loose fouling with a rag and cotton swabs
Pay attention to the breech face and extractor area

cleaning.name: BARREL AND LOCKING BLOCK
tasks: Bronze bore brush with solvent, six passes chamber to muzzle — NEVER a steel brush on the polygonal bore
Scrub the exterior of the barrel and the locking block with the nylon toothbrush

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING AND FRAME
tasks: Remove all visible fouling from the recoil spring assembly with solvent, a nylon brush or a rag and swabs
Scrub the frame where carbon is present, concentrating on the area normally covered by the slide
Wipe the frame rails and the disassembly lever

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Scrub the top of the magazine, concentrating on the follower and feed lips
Disassemble the magazine only for Major Cleaning
Check the follower slides freely and rises nearly flush against the feed lips

cleaning.name: INTERVALS
tasks: Normal cleaning after each firing or every twelve months, whichever comes first
Major cleaning after 500 cartridges, or after sand, dust, water — especially salt water — or other contaminants
Store and transport the pistol clean, lubricated, slide forward, and clean it at least every 12 months in storage

reassembly: Turn the slide upside down and insert the barrel with its angular locking surface facing upwards, then pivot the barrel rearward until the locking block snaps into the slide ejection port.
Insert the pronged end of the recoil spring into the tang on the slide above the muzzle.

Push the recoil spring forward, compressing it, then pivot the back of the guide rod onto the stepped mounting surface on the front of the barrel locking lug; the front of the spring must face forward.

Ensure no magazine is in the well and the disassembly lever is still down, then mount the slide onto the frame with the recoil spring centred under the barrel and the frame rails in the slide grooves.
Pull the slide back — pressing down on the rear of the slide if the rear frame insert does not pick up — and lock it back on either slide release.
Pivot the disassembly lever counterclockwise until it lies horizontal to the bottom of the slide.
fncheck: Clear the VP again, then rack the slide three or four times quickly and confirm it moves freely with no binding or locking. Return the slide forward, and with the pistol empty and pointed safely, pull the trigger and listen for an audible click. Rack the slide to the rear and release while holding the trigger back, then release the trigger and listen for the reset click that means the firing pin is engaged by the sear. Finally insert an empty magazine and rack: the slide must lock back on empty.
